## Pivotal Phase III Trial of Trastuzumab Plus Chemotherapy in HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer

The pivotal phase III trial, published by **Dennis Slamon and colleagues in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in 2001** (trial H0648g), was a landmark study that led to the FDA approval of trastuzumab (Herceptin) for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.

### Study Design and Patients

- **469 women** with previously untreated HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer were randomized to receive either **chemotherapy alone** or **chemotherapy plus trastuzumab**.
- Chemotherapy consisted of either an **anthracycline (doxorubicin or epirubicin) plus cyclophosphamide** or **paclitaxel**, depending on prior treatment history.
- Trastuzumab was administered concurrently with chemotherapy on a weekly basis.

### Efficacy / Survival Benefit

The addition of trastuzumab to chemotherapy produced statistically significant improvements across all major endpoints:

| Endpoint | Trastuzumab + Chemo | Chemo Alone | P-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Objective response rate** | 50% | 32% | < 0.001 |
| **Median duration of response** | 9.1 months | 6.1 months | < 0.001 |
| **Median time to disease progression** | 7.4 months | 4.6 months | — |
| **Median overall survival** | 25.1 months | 20.3 months | 0.046 |

The trial demonstrated an approximately **5-month improvement in median overall survival** with the addition of trastuzumab.

### Cardiac Side Effects

Cardiac dysfunction emerged as the most notable safety concern, particularly when trastuzumab was combined with anthracyclines:

- **Trastuzumab + anthracycline/cyclophosphamide**: **27% incidence** of cardiac dysfunction (with up to **16% experiencing NYHA class III/IV heart failure**).
- **Trastuzumab + paclitaxel**: **13% incidence** of cardiac dysfunction.
- **Trastuzumab alone** (from other studies): 3–7% incidence.
- By comparison, **anthracycline/cyclophosphamide alone** had an 8% rate, and **paclitaxel alone** had a 1% rate.

An independent **Cardiac Review and Evaluation Committee (CREC)** was subsequently formed to retrospectively review cardiac toxicity data across seven phase II and III trastuzumab studies (1,219 patients). The CREC defined cardiac dysfunction as a decrease in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), symptoms/signs of congestive heart failure (CHF), or a decline in LVEF of ≥5% (with symptoms) or ≥10% (without symptoms) to an absolute LVEF ≤55%. Importantly, most trastuzumab-treated patients who developed cardiac dysfunction were **symptomatic (75%)**, but the majority **improved with standard heart failure treatment (79%)**.

### Significance

This trial established that trastuzumab combined with chemotherapy significantly improved survival in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, but also highlighted the need for cardiac monitoring — especially when used alongside anthracyclines. The concurrent use of trastuzumab with anthracyclines is now generally avoided in clinical practice due to this cardiac risk.
